title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Proton conductivity in hydrophilic-channel POM all-inorganic frameworks increases sharply with relative humidity because water enters the channels and completes hydrogen-bond pathways.
explanation: The review repeats this trend for phosphate-linked {P4Mo6} framework Mo24b, the self-polymerized {Mo154} framework, and lanthanide-linked {MnV13} frameworks V13a and V13b. Mo154 conductivity exceeds that of low-dimensional {Mo154} compounds and is ascribed to continuous proton-hopping paths plus porosity. For V13a/b, D2O exchange was used to confirm the role of water. Mo24b remains durable over humidification cycles, and its high conductivity near 95 °C is tied to thermal stability and water retention in hydrophilic channels.
scope: Water-mediated proton conduction in open POM frameworks with hydrophilic channels, illustrated by Mo24b, Mo154, and V13a/V13b.
conditions: Variable relative humidity; Mo24b studied from about 40–98% RH and 25–95 °C; Mo154 impedance at different RH and temperature; V13a/b at 25 °C and 75–95% RH.
caveats: Not all frameworks in the review require mobile water: V7 shows appreciable proton conductivity under anhydrous conditions below the melting point of water. Humidity can also destabilize some PEG-containing Preyssler frameworks.
